landing.docTitle: Devotional Journal — Bilingual Bible study, focus, and encrypted journaling

hero.sub: A bilingual (EN/ES) Bible study companion for men who want consistency. Set a focus, follow AI-curated reading plans, and journal privately — encrypted end-to-end.

problem.quote: I want to be consistent in my faith — but I keep falling off.
problem.body: Most Bible apps are content libraries or social feeds. They don't help you build a daily rhythm. Devotional Journal is built around the habit loop — focus, read, journal, reflect, track.

how.heading: How it works
how.sub: Five small steps that compound into a real habit.

step1.title: Set a focus
step1.body: Pick what you're working through — anxiety, leadership, prayer life, anger.

step2.title: Read
step2.body: AI curates daily passages tied to your focus, in your translation.

step3.title: Journal
step3.body: Encrypted at rest. Mood-tagged. Only you can read it.

step4.title: Reflect
step4.body: Life-area scoring. AI threads follow up on what you wrestled with last week.

step5.title: Track
step5.body: Streaks, milestones, and a 30/60/90-day growth report you can export.

features.heading: Everything you need to build the habit
features.sub: No upsells. No social feed. No paywalled study guides. Just the tools to show up daily.

f1.title: AI-curated devotionals
f1.body: Set a focus, get daily scripture, prompts, and study guides personalized to it.

f2.title: Reading plans
f2.body: Browse pre-built plans or generate your own with AI from a single topic.

f3.title: Encrypted journal
f3.body: Per-user AES encryption. Even with database access, no one can read your entries.

f4.title: Built-in Bible reader
f4.body: KJV included. ASV, YLT, WEB, RVR1960 (Spanish) and more via the Bolls API.

f5.title: Open threads
f5.body: "Last week you mentioned anxiety about work. How's that going?" The AI remembers what you wrestled with.

f6.title: Streaks & milestones
f6.body: Confetti at milestones. Share cards for 3, 7, 30, 90, and 365 days.

f7.title: Bilingual to the bone
f7.body: Plans, themes, and prompts stored in EN and ES. Bilingual mode shows both side by side.

f8.title: Export everything
f8.body: Full ZIP backup or Markdown exports for journal, highlights, and growth reports.

f9.title: Self-host friendly
f9.body: Docker Compose stack. Runs on a Pi or any cloud VM. AGPL-3.0 licensed.

privacy.heading: Your reflections are yours
privacy.sub: Privacy isn't a marketing line here. The encryption code is open and the threat model is documented.
privacy.p1: Per-user AES encryption on every journal entry
privacy.p3: Bring your own AI — Ollama keeps everything local
privacy.p4: GDPR-style export and delete from your account
privacy.p5: Source code under AGPL-3.0 — audit it yourself
privacy.p6: Share cards never include journal text

shots.heading: A look inside
shots.sub: Designed to be calm, focused, and out of the way.

faq.heading: Frequently asked questions
faq.a1: The tone, prompts, and focus suggestions are written with men in mind — fathers, leaders, men in recovery, men building faith discipline. The features themselves work for anyone.
faq.q2: Do I need an OpenAI or Anthropic account?
faq.a2: No. You can run everything locally with Ollama. Your reflections never leave your network in that setup.
faq.q3: What happens if I lose my encryption key?
faq.a3: Every journal entry becomes unreadable forever. There is no recovery. Treat the key like a master password and back it up before anything else.
faq.a4: Yes. Settings → Export gives you a full ZIP and Markdown exports for journal, highlights, and a growth report.
faq.a5: A maintainer-run instance exists for personal use. There is no public hosted offering yet — self-host is the supported path.
faq.a6: Free. AGPL-3.0 licensed. If you self-host for others, your modifications must be open-sourced under the same license.

help.title: Help & Guide
help.intro: Everything this app does, where to find it, and what to do when something goes wrong.

step1.title: Open a new entry.
step1.body: Choose Journal, then New Entry — or press the round pen button at the bottom of any page.

step2.title: Write or speak.
step2.body: Type what's on your mind, or press Dictate and talk. It doesn't have to be about faith. Pick a mood if you like.

step3.title: Save.
step3.body: The app reads your entry and, within a few seconds to a minute or two, shows a reflection and a Bible passage.

step4.title: Read why.
step4.body: See why that passage was chosen and why it is worth meditating on. Open "Why this scripture?" for the full decision record.

step5.title: Come back.
step5.body: As you add entries, the feedback connects them, and Progress shows your themes and growth over time.

feedback.title: How feedback and scripture work
feedback.p1: When you save an entry, the AI reads it together with your mood, your current focus and themes from recent entries. It writes a short reflection and suggests Bible references that fit.
feedback.p2: The AI only suggests references. The verse text itself is always fetched from the Bible source — the World English Bible, a modern public-domain translation, with the King James Version as an offline fallback. A suggested reference that cannot be found in the Bible is discarded, so you never see a verse the AI made up. A "Verified" badge means the text shown was checked against that source.
feedback.p3: If the AI can't be reached, you still get a passage: built-in keyword rules pick one, and a notice says so. You can try again with the AI later.
feedback.p4: Every decision is recorded: which AI ran and where, what it was given, each passage it suggested and what happened to it.

voice.title: Voice entry
voice.p1: On a new entry or in Quick capture, press Dictate and speak. Your words are added to the text box where the cursor is; press Stop dictating when you're done, then edit the text if needed and save.
voice.p2: Voice entry works in Chrome, Edge and Safari. Firefox has no speech recognition, so the button is shown but disabled there. The first time, your browser asks for permission to use the microphone.

privacy.title: Privacy and where the AI runs
privacy.local: Local AI (Ollama): the AI runs on your own computer or network. Your entries never leave it.
privacy.cloud: Cloud AI (a provider you choose in Settings, with your own key): the text of an entry is sent to that provider to write the feedback.
privacy.consent: If this server's default AI is a cloud provider, nothing is sent to it until you turn on the consent switch in Settings. Until then, AI features show AI_CONSENT_REQUIRED.
privacy.encrypted: Your journal entries are encrypted at rest on the server.
privacy.export: You can export your data from Settings at any time.

troubleshooting.title: Troubleshooting
troubleshooting.intro: Error messages show a short code. Find it below to see what it means and what to do.
troubleshooting.refBody: Error messages also show a reference id (for example a1b2c3d4). Quote it, with the code, when you ask the person who runs this server for help — it lets them find the exact request in the server log.

NETWORK_ERROR.meaning: The app could not reach the server.
NETWORK_ERROR.fix: Check your internet connection (and the VPN or mesh network, if this is a private server), then try again.

TIMEOUT.meaning: The server took too long to answer.
TIMEOUT.fix: Try again. AI features on a local model can take a minute or two.

NOT_AUTHENTICATED.meaning: You are signed out, or your session has expired.
NOT_AUTHENTICATED.fix: Sign in again. Anything you had typed but not saved may need to be re-entered.

PERMISSION_DENIED.meaning: Your account does not have access to this item.
PERMISSION_DENIED.fix: Go back and open it from your own journal or plans.

NOT_FOUND.meaning: The item does not exist, or was deleted.
NOT_FOUND.fix: Go back and refresh the list.

VALIDATION_ERROR.meaning: Something in what was submitted is missing or not valid — for example an empty entry.
VALIDATION_ERROR.fix: Read the message, correct the field it names, and try again.

RATE_LIMITED.meaning: Too many requests were made in a short time.
RATE_LIMITED.fix: Wait a few minutes before trying again.

SERVER_ERROR.fix: Try again. If it keeps happening, report it with the reference id.

AI_UNAVAILABLE.meaning: The AI provider could not be reached. Your entry is still saved, and feedback falls back to built-in rules.
AI_UNAVAILABLE.fix: If you use Ollama, make sure it is running and reachable. Check Settings → AI Provider, then use "Try again with AI".

AI_TIMEOUT.meaning: The AI took too long to respond.
AI_TIMEOUT.fix: Try again. If it happens often, choose a smaller or faster model in Settings.

AI_NOT_CONFIGURED.meaning: An AI provider is selected but its key or model is missing.
AI_NOT_CONFIGURED.fix: Open Settings → AI Provider and fill in the missing key or model.

AI_CONSENT_REQUIRED.meaning: This server's default AI is a cloud provider, and you have not allowed your entries to be sent to it.
AI_CONSENT_REQUIRED.fix: Turn on the consent switch in Settings → AI Provider, or set up your own local provider instead.

AI_BAD_RESPONSE.meaning: The AI answered, but its answer could not be used.
AI_BAD_RESPONSE.fix: Try again. If it keeps happening, try a different model in Settings.

AI_URL_NOT_ALLOWED.meaning: The AI address entered in Settings was rejected for safety.
AI_URL_NOT_ALLOWED.fix: Check the base URL in Settings → AI Provider, or ask the person who runs this server which addresses are allowed.

SCRIPTURE_UNAVAILABLE.meaning: The Bible text source could not be reached.
SCRIPTURE_UNAVAILABLE.fix: Try again in a moment. The built-in King James text is used when it is available.

CLIENT_ERROR.meaning: Something unexpected happened in the app itself.
CLIENT_ERROR.fix: Reload the page. If it keeps happening, report it with what you were doing.
